newsitem.title: UK: LME copper option vols rise on upside call buying.
newsitem.headline: LME copper option vols rise on upside call buying.

text.p: LME copper option volatilities skated higher on renewed interest for upside calls while covering of options helped boost futures, traders said.
Turnover, however, has been relatively modest this week, except for a large lump in aluminium that was dismissed as a "give-up" between clearers.
In copper, the spotlight was on upside calls for June and the third quarter, with September $2,600 calls trading at a high of 19.5 percent volatility, dealers said.
This was two points higher than on Monday, one said.
"The $2,600 strike seem to be the focus...now that copper has broken out, a lot of people are finding they have holes in their books and are trying to fill them," one said.
He added there were still "lurking buyers" and another trader said there had been enquiry for $2,700 calls for July.
The call buying began on Tuesday, when open interest rose by 150 lots (3,750 tonnes) in July $2,550 calls and by 200 lots (5,000 tonnes) in $2,550 August calls, LME data showed.
On Wednesday, open interest at the $2,600 strike increased by 150 lots for July, August and September and on Thursday, buying was seen in $2,450-$2,600 calls for June through September.
Covering on the call options helped push futures prices higher, dealers said.
There has also been light selling of nearby puts, they added.
On Thursday morning, at-the-money (ATM) implied volatility for July was quoted at 18.5/20.5 percent, August at 17.5/18.5 percent and fourth quarter at 16.0/17.0 percent.
In aluminium, volatility firmed slightly for fourth quarter material on buying of $1,800 and $1,850 calls.

On Monday, LME aluminium options recorded a turnover of 29,797 lots, but open interest only rose by 2,126 lots, leaving the impression that the bulk of business was a transfer in positions, traders said.
ATM implied volatility for June was quoted at 16.0/19.0 percent and fourth quarter at around 15.0/17.0 percent, up one-half to one point.
If three month prices can break through the peak so far this year at around $1,700, some players would gun for $1,800 where it is rumoured there are some large short option positions, a trader said.
Vols were largely unchanged on the other metals.
In zinc, there had been modest upside call buying linked to recent gains in futures and in tin, some interest in downside puts at $5,500 for the third quarter, traders said.
